record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Explain the origin of intermittency, meaning deviations from Kolmogorov scaling in velocity correlators, in fully developed turbulence.

evidence.quote: However an explanation of the origin of intermittency in the general case of developed turbulence remains one of the main open problems of theoretical hydrodynamics.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an incompressible fluid in three spatial dimensions whose velocity field $u(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^3$, $x\in\mathbb{R}^3$, satisfies the Navier–Stokes equations
\[ \partial_t u + (u\cdot\nabla)u = -\nabla p + \nu \Delta u + f, \qquad \nabla\cdot u = 0, \]
where $\nu>0$ is the kinematic viscosity and $f$ is a statistically homogeneous, isotropic random forcing acting at a large integral scale $L$. Assume the flow reaches a statistically stationary, homogeneous, isotropic state in the limit of vanishing viscosity (equivalently, infinite Reynolds number), giving rise to fully developed turbulence with an inertial range of scales $\eta \ll r \ll L$ (where $\eta$ is the dissipative Kolmogorov scale).

Define the longitudinal velocity structure functions of order $p \ge 1$ by
\[ S_p(r) \;=\; \big\langle\, \big( [u(x+r e) - u(x)] \cdot e \big)^{\,p} \,\big\rangle, \qquad e = r/|r|, \]
where $\langle\cdot\rangle$ denotes the ensemble (or space–time) average in the stationary state.

Kolmogorov's 1941 self-similarity theory predicts that in the inertial range
\[ S_p(r) \;\sim\; C_p\, (\varepsilon r)^{p/3}, \]
where $\varepsilon$ is the mean energy dissipation rate, so that the scaling exponents $\zeta_p$ defined by $S_p(r)\sim r^{\zeta_p}$ satisfy $\zeta_p = p/3$. Experimental and numerical evidence, however, shows systematic deviations from this linear law for $p\neq 3$: the measured exponents $\zeta_p$ form a strictly concave function of $p$ with $\zeta_p < p/3$ for $p>3$ and $\zeta_p > p/3$ for $p<3$. This phenomenon is called intermittency.

Problem. Derive, from the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations with a generic large-scale random forcing, a mathematical explanation of the origin of intermittency in fully developed three-dimensional turbulence. Specifically, establish the existence of the infinite-Reynolds-number statistically stationary state, prove that the structure functions $S_p(r)$ exhibit power-law behavior $S_p(r)\sim r^{\zeta_p}$ in an inertial range, and compute (or rigorously characterize) the anomalous scaling exponents $\zeta_p$, showing that $\zeta_p \neq p/3$ for $p\neq 3$.
artifact.status_search_result: The origin of intermittency and the anomalous scaling exponents of velocity structure functions in fully developed three-dimensional turbulence is widely regarded as a major open problem in theoretical hydrodynamics and mathematical physics. While phenomenological models (multifractal, She–Leveque, shell models) and rigorous results for passive scalar (Kraichnan) models exist, no derivation of the anomalous exponents $\zeta_p$ from the Navier–Stokes equations is known.

status_evidence.title: Frisch, Turbulence: The Legacy of A. N. Kolmogorov
status_evidence.snippet: Intermittency corrections to Kolmogorov's 1941 scaling remain a central unsolved problem.
status_evidence.claim: Anomalous scaling of velocity structure functions in 3D Navier–Stokes turbulence is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Falkovich, Gawedzki, Vergassola — Particles and fields in fluid turbulence, Rev. Mod. Phys. (2001)
status_evidence.snippet: While anomalous scaling has been understood for passive scalars, the case of the velocity field itself remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The origin of intermittency in the velocity field of Navier–Stokes turbulence is open.
